# prism-google Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Google: Decides whether the owner's browser may make one call to the Gmail or Google Calendar API, so that nothing is fetched while the Prism is halted, no other host is ever called, nothing is fetched without a fresh token the owner granted, and nothing is sent or changed without the owner's own act.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because when the owner presses the kill switch nothing may be fetched (constitution P7).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly fresh none yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when service is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is other, because the owner's token must never reach any host but the two Google APIs.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `other read readonly fresh owner no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never fetch when method is write and act is none

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when method is write and act is none, because no mail is sent and no calendar entry changed without the owner's act.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail write readonly fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `ask`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never fetch when token is none

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when token is none, because no call is made without a token the owner granted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly none none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `consent`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never fetch when token is expired

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when token is expired, because an expired grant is not the owner's consent.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar read readonly expired none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `consent`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never fetch when scope is none

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when scope is none, because no call is made to a service the owner did not grant.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read none fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `consent`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never fetch when method is write and scope is readonly

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when method is write and scope is readonly, because a read-only grant never sends or changes anything.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail write readonly fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `ask`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-001 refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because stop means stop (kill switch).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly fresh none yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 refuse when service is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when service is other and no earlier rule matches, because the page calls only the two Google APIs it names.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `other read readonly fresh owner no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 ask when method is write and act is none

The app SHALL answer `ask` when method is write and act is none and no earlier rule matches, because nothing is sent or changed without the owner's act.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail write readonly fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `ask`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 consent when token is not fresh

The app SHALL answer `consent` when token is not fresh and no earlier rule matches, because a call needs a fresh token the owner granted.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly none none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `consent`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 consent when scope is none

The app SHALL answer `consent` when scope is none and no earlier rule matches, because a call needs the owner's grant for this service.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read none fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `consent`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 consent when method is write and scope is not write

The app SHALL answer `consent` when method is write and scope is not write and no earlier rule matches, because a read-only grant never covers a write.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail write readonly fresh owner no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `consent`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 fetch when method is read

The app SHALL answer `fetch` when method is read and no earlier rule matches, because the owner granted reading.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly fresh none no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fetch`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 fetch when act is owner

The app SHALL answer `fetch` when act is owner and no earlier rule matches, because the owner pressed the button for this write.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar write write fresh owner no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fetch`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Otherwise refuse

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when no rule matches, because deny by default.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** a request meets the conditions above
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `gmail read readonly fresh none yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `fetch`, `consent`, `ask`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | `gmail`, `calendar`, `other` | which API the call goes to: the Gmail API, the Google Calendar API, or any other host |
| `method` | `read`, `write` | whether the call only reads (GET) or would send, create, change or delete something |
| `scope` | `none`, `readonly`, `write` | the access the owner granted Google for this service: none, read only, or read and write |
| `token` | `none`, `fresh`, `expired` | the access token the page holds in memory for this service |
| `act` | `none`, `owner` | whether the owner pressed the button for this very call |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner has pressed the kill switch |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch` | the page may make the call now |
| `consent` | the page must first ask Google for the owner's consent and a fresh token |
| `ask` | the owner must act first |
| `refuse` | the call may not be made |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- It does not hold or see the token; the page keeps it in memory and reports only whether it is fresh.
- It does not decide what is kept: every fetched item still goes through the Boundary and the vault.
- The act field is set only by the owner's own press of a button for that call.
- The page asks only for read-only scopes today, so every write is refused for want of a write grant.

## Examples

- `gmail read readonly fresh none no` gives `fetch`
- `calendar read readonly fresh none no` gives `fetch`
- `gmail read readonly fresh none yes` gives `refuse`
- `other read readonly fresh owner no` gives `refuse`
- `gmail read readonly none none no` gives `consent`
- `calendar read readonly expired none no` gives `consent`
- `gmail read none fresh none no` gives `consent`
- `gmail write readonly fresh none no` gives `ask`
- `gmail write readonly fresh owner no` gives `consent`
- `calendar write write fresh owner no` gives `fetch`
- `calendar write write fresh none no` gives `ask`
- `gmail write write expired owner no` gives `consent`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
